gap: No result ChatGPT got states that SteelSeries says the Arctis Nova 5 and Nova 5P won't work with Xbox even if you buy the Nova 5X dongle separately, so the headset itself has to be the 5X, and a spare or second-hand 5X dongle won't help.
standout_why: I could not read the picks on the two cited rivals. RTINGS (https://www.rtings.com/headphones/reviews/best/xbox-series-x) loads its picks with JavaScript, and WebFetch got only 3,517 characters of navigation. On Tom's Guide (https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-gaming-headsets), the parts I fetched at offsets 0, 8,000 and 12,000 were menus with no headset text. So I can't say whether they mention version exclusions. The uncited top-10 result Adellion (https://adellion.com/xbox-headsets-under-150) covers part of this: 'their PlayStation versions will not connect to an Xbox' and 'buy the Xbox version'. It does not cover the maker-stated point that moving the dongle doesn't fix it (Nova 5/5P plus a 5X dongle still fails). It also has no Turtle Beach Support statement and doesn't explain the Xbox/USB switch on the dongle. ChatGPT's own answer only says 'choose an Xbox-compatible model'.
decides: This confirms the wireless picks only if the exact Xbox SKU is the one bought: Arctis Nova 5X (not Nova 5 or 5P) and Stealth 600 Gen 3 'for Xbox' (not the PlayStation version). Both Xbox SKUs also work on PlayStation and PC, so for a mixed-console home the Xbox SKU is the one to buy. The Xbox Wireless Headset needs no dongle but works only on Xbox, Windows and Bluetooth phones. Wired picks (EKSA Fenrir S, Xbox Stereo Headset) plug into the controller's 3.5 mm jack instead.

findings.label: Which Nova 5 models work on Xbox
findings.value: Only the Nova 5X. 'The Nova 5 and Nova 5P won't work with Xbox—even if you'd purchase the Nova 5X dongle separately.'
findings.source_title: Nova 5 Connection Issues Troubleshooting – SteelSeries Support
findings.note: Maker's support article, quoted word for word. It also says: 'The Arctis Nova 5X is the only Nova 5 model built for Xbox.'

findings.label: Dongle switch setting for Xbox
findings.value: Switch set to 'Xbox' for Xbox Series X|S or Xbox One; 'USB' for PC, PlayStation or other platforms
findings.source_title: Nova 5 Connection Issues Troubleshooting – SteelSeries Support
findings.note: Same maker article. If the switch is in the wrong position, the headset won't connect to the console.

findings.label: Works on Xbox?
findings.value: No. 'The Stealth 600 Gen 3 for PlayStation will NOT work on any Xbox console.'
findings.source_title: Best Buy Q&A – Turtle Beach Stealth 600 (PS5/PS4/PC/Mobile, White)
findings.note: The answer is signed by Turtle Beach Support (the maker), not a shopper. It adds: 'the Stealth 600 Gen 3 for Xbox ... will work on both Xbox and PlayStation.'

findings.label: Transmitter reach, Xbox version vs PlayStation version
findings.value: Xbox version: a transmitter with a mode-switching button works with Xbox, PlayStation and PC. PlayStation version: PlayStation and PC only.
findings.source_title: Turtle Beach Stealth 600 Gen 3 review – SoundGuys
findings.note: Named reviewer SoundGuys. The same review measured 83 h 42 min of battery against the 80 h claimed.

findings.label: Maker compatibility list, box contents and price
findings.value: Xbox Series X|S and Xbox One; PS5 and PS4; Windows 10+ PC (USB 2.0+); Bluetooth 5.2 mobile. In the box: USB wireless transmitter (USB-A per the FAQ) and a 0.7 m USB-A to USB-C charging cable. $109.99.
findings.source_title: Stealth 600 Wireless Gaming Headset – Turtle Beach
findings.note: The page has a single platform selector (Xbox/PlayStation/PC) and shows one full price of $109.99. It doesn't list separate prices per platform.

findings.label: Compatible devices and requirements
findings.value: Xbox Series X|S, Xbox One, Windows 10/11, and mobile devices with Bluetooth. 'Windows 10/11 use requires Bluetooth 4.2+ or compatible USB-C cable.' 'Some voice chat features may require XBOX Game Pass Ultimate, Premium, or Essential.' Battery up to 20 h.
findings.note: PlayStation is not on the compatible list. The page shows no price ('may vary by retailer').

findings.label: Connection and compatible devices
findings.value: Plugs into the Xbox Wireless Controller's 3.5 mm jack, no batteries. Xbox Series X|S, Xbox One, and Windows 10/11 devices with a 3.5 mm jack. 10 oz (286 g).
findings.note: No price on the maker page.

findings.label: Plug standard for wired 3.5 mm headsets on Xbox (Microsoft adapter)
findings.value: 'Any 3.5mm stereo headset (that uses the CTIA plug standard) can get stereo game audio by plugging into the adapter.' The Xbox One Stereo Headset Adapter launched at $24.99 MSRP.
findings.source_title: Xbox One Stereo Headset and Headset Adapter Details – Xbox Wire
findings.note: Maker announcement from 2014. The $24.99 is the launch MSRP, not a price checked today.

findings.label: Connection and price
findings.value: 3.5 mm wired, 'compatible with multi-platform devices with 3.5mm audio jacks'. Also has a USB connector and a Y-splitter cable. $36.99.
findings.source_title: EKSA® Fenrir S Xbox Gaming Headset
findings.note: Price from storecheck.py on eksa.net (Shopify), shown as available. The page doesn't say the USB plug carries audio, so for Xbox treat it as 3.5 mm into the controller.

unsourced: A Microsoft document listing which Xbox One controllers have no 3.5 mm jack and need the Stereo Headset Adapter. Only iFixit and parts sellers name model 1537, and I found no Microsoft or support.xbox.com page. support.xbox.com/en-US/help/hardware-network/accessories/xbox-wireless-headset returned only its heading.

HyperX Cloud III: how it connects to Xbox (3.5 mm vs USB) and whether DTS/USB audio works on Xbox. hyperx.com returned HTTP 429 three times.
